issues.description: The solution's assembleBookstore function signature does not match the expected no-argument signature shown in the template and implied by the problem statement. In Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift the main() calls assembleBookstore() with no parameters, but the solution defines private static func assembleBookstore(seed: Double) -> Bookstore which requires a Double argument. The template's commented signature expects assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore (no parameters). This mismatch will cause a compile-time error and confuses students about the correct function signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the function signature and its usage. Either remove the seed: Double parameter from the solution's assembleBookstore so it becomes private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore (matching the template and the call), or update the main call and the template to pass a Double argument and document the parameter in the problem statement. The simplest fix is to remove the seed parameter so the signature matches the intended no-argument assembleBookstore().

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an assembleBookstore() function with no parameters, but the solution implements assembleBookstore(seed: Double) -> Bookstore (a different signature). This parameter mismatch for the same conceptual function creates confusion: students mapping the requirement 'Implement assembleBookstore' to the provided solution will encounter a different method signature and may be unsure which form is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the assembleBookstore signature consistent across artifacts. Either remove the unused seed parameter in the solution and use: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore, or modify the template/problem to document the seed parameter (and provide a default value such as seed: Double = 0.0) so all three artifacts share the same function signature. Ensure all call sites are updated accordingly.
